answer.decision: Use field-specific merge rules with monotonic account-status precedence and version metadata.
answer.action: Automatically merge profile fields using deterministic version metadata and unique operation IDs. Treat suspended as dominating active regardless of wall-clock order, and permit reactivation only through an explicit reviewed unsuspend operation. Reconcile queued operations after partitions with idempotent processing.
reasons: This prevents stale replicated data from changing an account from suspended to active.
Field-specific deterministic merging allows ordinary profile conflicts to converge automatically.
Both regions remain writable during partitions, satisfying business-continuity requirements.
Wall-clock last-write-wins is unsafe because observed regional clock skew has reached 47 seconds.
Existing unique operation IDs and the ability to identify reviewed unsuspend operations support deterministic, idempotent reconciliation.
assumptions: Version metadata can represent causal or deterministic ordering without relying solely on wall-clock timestamps.
The reviewed unsuspend operation is authenticated, auditable, and explicitly overrides the normal suspended-dominates-active rule.
Profile fields do not independently carry authorization consequences equivalent to account status.
risks: Incorrect implementation of status precedence or unsuspend detection could create an authorization vulnerability.
Concurrent edits to the same profile field may converge deterministically while still selecting a value users did not intend.
Version metadata retention, tombstones, and replay handling require careful lifecycle management.
A compromised or duplicated reviewed-unsuspend workflow could bypass the monotonic safety rule unless authorization and idempotency are enforced.

citations.claim: Suspended status must dominate stale active data, except through an explicit reviewed unsuspend operation that the resolver can distinguish.
Profile conflicts are rare and must converge automatically.
Both regions must remain writable during partitions lasting up to one hour.
Past clock skew of 47 seconds makes wall-clock last-write-wins unsafe.
Unique operation IDs are already attached to writes and can support idempotent reconciliation.
